summary: TundraHealth prod: routing circuit-breaker tripped -> cascade fallbacks, P0 customer escalation
description:
Issue summary:
On 2025-11-14 at ~07:12 UTC TundraHealth reported elevated 5xx rates and long tail generation latency for realtime chat requests. Customers saw streaming disconnects and sporadic 502/504s. The initial spike coincided with a scheduled traffic migration for the customer's dedicated pool.

Impact:
- Customer-facing P0: multiple endpoints producing 20-40% 5xx and streaming truncation for ~45 minutes.
- User sessions terminated mid-stream; some completions duplicated after retries.
- Root symptoms appeared in smart-routing circuit-breaker tripping and fallback to quantized variants, increasing long-tail latency and causing autoscaler churn in the dedicated pool.

Timeline (condensed):
- 07:10 UTC: TundraHealth reports increased error/rate of truncations via support channel.
- 07:12 UTC: Pager alerts generated for elevated 5xx in us-east-1 serving-runtime.
- 07:15 UTC: Support triage calls SRE and Eng; customer escalates to P0.
- 07:18 UTC: Observed circuit-breaker on smart-routing triggered; large fraction of requests routed to fallback model (quantized).
- 07:20-07:35 UTC: Dedicated GPU autoscaler oscillation observed (scale up/down thrash), causing worker churn and increased error surface.
- 07:40 UTC: Hotfix to routing policy rolled (raise CB threshold + sticky routing to warmed pools).
- 08:05 UTC: Error rates return to baseline; streaming verified end-to-end.
- 11:00 UTC: Full verification and customer confirmation; incident paged as resolved.

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) On a dedicated pool with warm-up disabled, replay a spike of 2.5x steady QPS with a small fraction (5-10%) of artificially long inference requests (seq len > 1k).
2) Force smart-routing latency on primary model by injecting 500ms p99 delay on a subset of replicas.
3) Observe circuit-breaker tripping and routing to quantized variant; watch autoscaler for scale events.

Observed logs and metrics excerpts:
- smart-routing: circuit_breaker.trip_rate=0.32, cb_reason=upstream_latency
- serving-runtime: 502 and 504 spike correlating with model-switch events
- scheduler: scale_events=7 within 15m window, avg_pod_warm_time=38s
- customer-reported traces: session_id=th-9c3a streamed cutoff at token 412

Attachments/References:
- Support Slack thread: #support -> thread ts: 1709962345.000200
- Incident channel: #incidents/inc-2025-11-14-07
- Related GitHub PR / infra change: github.com/redwood/inference-runtime/pull/1423
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: configuration mismatch in circuit-breaker thresholds for dedicated customers combined with recently deployed autoscaler tuning. Investigation found smart-routing CB was set to an aggressive failover threshold for dedicated pools during the migration; when a small subset of replicas reported elevated latency (due to warm cache misses), the CB tripped and routed high volume to quantized fallback. The quantized variant had higher p99 under these mixed loads because it was cold and not warm-cached; this increased overall latency and triggered autoscaler scale-up which then caused more cold starts (feedback loop). No code-level memory corruption or kernel faults were found. Logs showed rapid model-switch churn correlating with scale events.

Key findings:
- CB thresholds for dedicated pools were using global defaults that are too aggressive for workloads with bursty long-sequence requests.
- Dedicated autoscaler policy had a short cool-down (60s) and small scale increments leading to oscillation under mixed latency conditions.
- Fallback model was not sufficiently warmed for sudden traffic increases.
resolution_notes:
Applied a staged mitigation: 1) Increased circuit-breaker window and trip threshold for dedicated pools (config change rolled at 07:40 UTC). 2) Applied sticky routing to keep requests on warmed replicas when possible. 3) Temporary manual capacity bump for TundraHealth's dedicated pool (2x for 30 minutes) to absorb residual requests. 4) Added a short warm-up run for quantized variants when first routed. 5) Adjusted autoscaler cooldown to 180s and increased scale step to reduce flapping.
Post-recovery validation: synthetic load tests and customer traffic replays run from 08:15-09:30 UTC showed error rates within SLA and stable p99 latency. Customer confirmed end-to-end on 11:00 UTC. No rollback of model versions was necessary.
follow_up_actions: Create formal runbook update: add dedicated-pool circuit-breaker baseline for bursty seq workloads (owner: SRE - due 2025-11-22)
Implement automated warm-up for quantized fallback variants when traffic volume crosses 200rps for >30s (owner: Runtime team - PR: #1423)
Adjust autoscaler default cooldown and step policy for dedicated pools across regions (owner: Infra - due 2025-11-28)
Customer remediation: one month of service credit applied and 2 dedicated hours of solutions architecture support scheduled (owner: CS)
RCA doc and post-incident review scheduled in Confluence and ops-all-hands (owner: Eng - meeting 2025-11-20)
Add targeted alert: CB trip rate >0.1 for 5m for dedicated pools in us-east-1 (owner: Monitoring)
Run a chaos test simulating cold start + burst traffic for dedicated pools in staging (owner: Reliability - due 2025-12-05)
